_meta.purpose: Research extraction for how far back RMS dashboard charts can honestly reach.
_meta.note: All figures below were read directly from the cited primary-source PDFs (company press releases / financial reports), not interpolated. Amounts in EUR million unless stated.

quarterly_revenue_total.earliest_published: Q1 2016 (and further back; Q1 2015/Q3 2015 press releases also retrieved and resolve at assets-finance.hermes.com, but the 2015 half-year/full-year press releases under the same legacy naming scheme returned HTTP 401 -- only the half-year FINANCIAL REPORT and ANNUAL REPORT for 2012-2015 resolve)
quarterly_revenue_total.evidence: hermes_2016_CA1T_en.pdf (Q1 2016, filed 2016-04-28) prints Q1 2016 AND Q1 2015 side by side; the site's own publications-table UI only lists years back to 2017, but the legacy asset path (.../pdf_file/2020-06/hermes_<year>_<doc>_en.pdf) still serves 2016 and 2015 Q1/Q3 releases (HTTP 200) even though the UI does not show them.

quarterly_revenue_by_sector_7way.structural_note: The 7-sector split (Leather Goods & Saddlery / Ready-to-wear & Accessories / Silk & Textiles / Other Hermès sectors / Perfumes(->Perfume and Beauty) / Watches / Other products) is identical in name and scope from Q1 2016 through the current site. Only the Perfumes label changed to 'Perfume and Beauty' between the FY2020 and FY2022 releases (no revenue break, cosmetic rename only).

quarterly_revenue_by_region_6way.structural_break: The 'Other' region line was renamed 'Other (Middle East)' by the FY2024 release (published 2025-02-14), which also states: 'Hermès became a majority shareholder in January 2024 alongside its partner in the Middle East in the retail activities located in the United Arab Emirates. As a reminder, the impact resulting from this acquisition of a majority stake was not significant on the 2024 consolidated financial statements.' Despite that 'not significant' group-level characterization, the region's own reported revenue line jumped +109.7% published / +109.6% constant-currency in FY2024 (627 vs 299), i.e. this specific series has a consolidation-scope break at FY2024 even though the company frames the group-level impact as immaterial.

constant_currency_growth.earliest_published: Q1 2016 (printed as its own column in every release since at least 2016; the two-year historical Q1 2018 vs Q1 2017 table confirms continuity)

half_yearly_operating_profit_and_margin_.earliest_published: H1 2016 (and the H1 2016 release's own 'Key figures' table additionally reprints FY2015 and H1 2015, so the group-level series is directly readable back to H1 2015)
half_yearly_operating_profit_and_margin_.structural_break: H1 2016 half-year financial report, Note 6/Note 7: 'On 30 June 2016, to enhance the understanding of the income statement, the Group decided to recognise free share plan expense at €21.1 million under the item "Other operating incomes & expenses". If this expense had been classified in "Selling, marketing and administrative expenses" in June 2015, the "Other operating incomes & expenses" would have amounted to €104.3 million instead of €86.7 million, and the "Selling, marketing and administrative expenses" to €676.3 million instead of €693.9 million.' This means any margin-bridge decomposition that separates SG&A from 'other income/expenses' (the page's EX_MARGIN_BRIDGE-style chart) cannot be run on a like-for-like basis before H1 2016 without adjusting for this reclassification -- H1 2016 is a genuine structural floor for that specific decomposition, not merely a research-effort floor.

half_yearly_operating_profit_by_region_s.earliest_published: H1 2016 (Note 4.1 'Information by operating segment', with FY2015 and H1 2015 comparatives printed in the same note)
half_yearly_operating_profit_by_region_s.evidence: H1 2016 and H1 2018 half-year financial reports (Note 4) both give revenue, SG&A, D&A, operating provisions, impairment losses, other income/expenses, recurring operating income, operating margin by segment, and (from 2018) operating investments, by the same 6 geographic segments (France / Europe ex-France / Japan / Asia-Pacific ex-Japan / Americas / Other) plus a Holding column -- structurally identical to the current h1_segments schema.

adjusted_free_cash_flow.earliest_published: Not published as a discrete line before FY2018 ('Free cash flow' first appears in the FY2018 key-figures table: 1,447 vs 1,340 for FY2017); it becomes 'Adjusted free cash flow' from the FY2019 release onward with a definition footnote ('sum of operating cash flows and change in working capital requirement, less operating investments and repayment of lease liabilities, as per IFRS cash flow statement').
adjusted_free_cash_flow.retrievable_now: From FY2018 (as plain 'Free cash flow') and FY2019 onward (as 'Adjusted free cash flow'); not available as a company-published figure for FY2016/FY2017 or earlier -- a null with this reason, not an omission.

chart_reachability.title_cn: 上半年经常性经营利润率拆解（毛利率/SG&A/D&A/减值/免费股/残值）
chart_reachability.kind: bridge_bar, single half-year snapshot (not currently a timeline, but re-runnable each half)
chart_reachability.reason_if_not_2016: This is the one exhibit with a genuine, company-stated accounting-classification floor, not just a data-availability floor: the free-share-plan expense line moved from 'Selling, marketing and administrative expenses' into 'Other operating incomes & expenses' exactly at H1 2016 (H1 2016 half-year financial report, Note 6/7, quoted above). Before H1 2016, the SG&A/other-income split this bridge depends on is measured on a different basis, so a bridge computed pre- and post- H1 2016 without adjustment would silently mix two accounting bases. Honest options: start the bridge at H1 2016, or -- if extending earlier -- apply the company's own stated pro-forma adjustment for the one comparative half (H1 2015) it disclosed, and go no further back than that, since no such pro-forma exists for years before H1 2015.
'Investments (excluding financial investments)' / 'Operating investments' is printed in every H1 and FY key-figures table back through 2016 (confirmed H1 2016: 107.6; FY2016: 285.4).

structural_breaks.what: Free-share-plan expense reclassified from SG&A into 'Other operating incomes & expenses'.
structural_breaks.company_wording: On 30 June 2016, to enhance the understanding of the income statement, the Group decided to recognise free share plan expense at €21.1 million under the item "Other operating incomes & expenses". If this expense had been classified in "Selling, marketing and administrative expenses" in June 2015, the "Other operating incomes & expenses" would have amounted to €104.3 million instead of €86.7 million, and the "Selling, marketing and administrative expenses" to €676.3 million instead of €693.9 million.
structural_breaks.affects: Any margin-bridge chart that separates SG&A from other income/expenses (EX_MARGIN_BRIDGE-style).

structural_breaks.what: IFRS 16 (Leases) adopted retrospectively; FY2018/H1 2018 recurring operating income and margin restated upward.
structural_breaks.evidence: FY2019 release: 'FY 2018 restated' recurring operating income 2,075 (34.8% margin) vs FY2018-as-first-published 2,045 (34.3%); footnote: '2018 restatements relate to the application of the IFRS 16 - Leases standard on a retrospective basis.' Same restatement appears for H1 2018 in the H1 2019 release (996 restated vs 984.5 as first published).

structural_breaks.what: Hermès became majority shareholder of its Middle East retail partner (UAE); 'Other' region relabeled 'Other (Middle East)' and its revenue roughly doubled on a published and constant-currency basis.
structural_breaks.company_wording: Hermès became a majority shareholder in January 2024 alongside its partner in the Middle East in the retail activities located in the United Arab Emirates. As a reminder, the impact resulting from this acquisition of a majority stake was not significant on the 2024 consolidated financial statements.
structural_breaks.evidence: FY2024 release: Other (Middle East) 627 (2024) vs 299 (2023), +109.7% published / +109.6% cc.
structural_breaks.affects: The 6th region series specifically; group-level totals are, by the company's own account, not materially affected.

structural_breaks.what: Sector label 'Perfumes' renamed 'Perfume and Beauty' (no scope change detected in the revenue figures across the rename).
'Free cash flow' introduced as a disclosed metric at FY2018; renamed 'Adjusted free cash flow' with a stated formula from FY2019 onward. Not published for FY2016/FY2017.
